headline: Welcome to the live coverage of stage 9 of La Vuelta 26
subtext: Onto week 2! After the first rest day, La Vuelta 26 resumes action with a rolling stage between Alcaraz and Elche de la Sierra (184.7 km) with three categorised climbs and almost 3,000 metres of elevation across the day’s many hills. The neutral start is set at 12:45, the start proper at 12:59 after a 6.2 km parade, and the winners should be crowned at around 17:30.

headline: Unprecedented La Vuelta stage towns in a familiar area
subtext: Alcaraz and Elche de la Sierra stage towns making their first appearance in La Vuelta this year. The full list: Monaco (stage 1), Manosque (2), Font-Romeu (stage 3), Falset (5), Roquetes (5), Vall d’Alba (7), Puçol (8), Xeraco (8), La Vila Joiosa (9), Alcaraz (10), Elche de la Sierra (10), Vera (12), Almuñécar (13), Palma del Rio (15), Cortegana (16), La Rábida (16), Dos Hermanas (17), El Puerto de Santa María (18), La Calahorra (20), and Collado del Aguacil (20). Elche de la Sierra hosted the start of stage 3 of La Vuelta Femenina by Carrefour.es 23. Wearing La Roja as the overall leader, Marianne Vos sprinted to victory in La Roda. This is the first La Vuelta stage in the province of Albacete since Jasper Philipsen’s victory in Albacete on stage 5 of La Vuelta 2021. Kenny Elissonde took La Roja.

headline: 2 birthday boys in the peloton
subtext: Eddie Dunbar (Pinarello Q36.5) turns 30 years old today while Embret Svestad-Bardseng (Netcompany Ineos) celebrates his 24th birthday. The Irishman took two stage wins in 2024. As for the Norwegian youngster, this is first participation. He was in the breakaway yesterday and currently is 21st overall. Today is also the 32nd birthday of Riejanne Markus, second of La Vuelta Femenina by Carrefour.es. Juan Santiago Zurano was also born on September 1st, in 1948. He won stage 14 of La Vuelta in 1974, in Bilbao.

headline: Herrada: "My brother and I have come here to train loads of times in this area"
subtext: Hailing from Mota del Cuervo, 100 kilometres north of Alcaraz, Jesus Herrada (Burgos-Burpellet-BH) is riding his final La Vuelta stage in Castilla-La Mancha: “I’m really looking forward to it. We’ve had a rest day, so we’ve recharged our batteries. It’s a stage I know very well; my brother and I have come here to train loads of times in this area. I’m very fond of this stage. My home, my village, is just over an hour away from here. So we’re hoping to see lots of people at the start, along the route and at the finish. It’s going to be an interesting and entertaining day because we don’t know what might happen – whether a large breakaway might form or if there’s a team capable of controlling the race on this terrain. After all, the total elevation gain is nearly 3,000 metres. There aren’t any major mountain passes, but it goes up and down all day. So it’s going to be a great day.”

headline: Let’s roll
subtext: The peloton make their way to the start proper with a 6.2 km parade.

headline: 2 non-starters
subtext: There are 168 riders in the peloton as George Bennett (NSN) and Henri-François Renard-Haquin (Picnic PostNL) don't start.

headline: La Roja
subtext: Enric Mas (Movistar) stamped his authority with a stage win at Alto de Aitana and he enters week 2 with la Roja on his back. The Spaniard leads the overall standings with a gap of 1’18’’ to Primoz Roglic (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) and 1’39’’ to Felix Gall (Decathlon CMA CGM). Oscar Onley (Netcompany Ineos) is fourth, trailing by 2’20’’.

headline: Green jersey
subtext: Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) is a solid leader of the points standings with a tally of 124. His teammate Matthew Brennan is second with 67 points. Mads Pedersen (Lidl-Trek) follows with 58 points.

headline: Wout van Aert, Enric Mas, Oscar Onley
Polka dot jersey
subtext: Santiago Buitrago is the first Colombian leader of the mountains standings of La Vuelta since Nairo Quintana after stages 11 and 12 in 2016. At the time, Quintana was wearing La Roja. The last Colombian rider to wear the polka dot jersey during a La Vuelta stage is Walter Pedraza on day 3 in 2015. His compatriot Esteban Chaves was leading the mountains standings but he raced with La Roja. Buitrago has 29 points, five more than Enric Mas (Movistar). Andreas Leknessund (Uno-X Mobility) follows with 19 points.

headline: White jersey
subtext: Oscar Onley (Netcompany Ineos) pulled away from his rivals at the top of the young riders standings. The British climber is now 5’45’’ ahead of Jakob Omrzel (Bahrain Victorious), while Jarno Widar (Lotto Intermarché) trails by 7’14’’.

headline: Team standings
subtext: With Felix Gall (4th), Gregor Muhlberger (12th) and Matthew Riccitello (16th) battling at the front up the Alto de Aitana, Decathlon CMA CGM extended their lead in the team standings to 42’30’’ on Netcompany Ineos and 49’34’’ on Visma-Lease a Bike.

headline: Combativity award
subtext: Pavel Sivakov (UAE Emirates XRG) will race with a distinctive bib today as he was named the most combative rider en route to the Alto de Aitana.

headline: Stage 10 is ON!
subtext: The battle resumes with a rolling stage!

headline: First attacks
subtext: A lone attacker leads the way at km 2.

headline: More movement
subtext: The loneleader was caught at km 3. It's a four-rider group leading the way.

headline: Make it 6 leaders
subtext: They're at km 5. The gap is very small.

headline: The attackers are caught at km 6
subtext: Today could favour fast men or long range attackers depending on the scenario. Many riders said the dynamics at the start will be key to establish the race scenario.

headline: Attacks keep flying...
subtext: But the bunch is packed at km 8.

headline: 6 leaders: Vine, Cort, Herrada...
subtext: Domen Novak, Jay Vine (UAE Emirates XRG), Rémy Rochas (Groupama-FDJ United), Magnus Cort (Uno-X Mobility), Finlay Pickering (Jayco AlUla) and Jesus Herrada (Burgos Burpellet BH) are 12 seconds ahead of the bunch.

headline: Back together again
subtext: How long will it take for the breakaway to establish? The answer to that question will also determine their chances of making it to the end.

headline: 6 new leaders
subtext: Enzo Paleni (Groupama-FDJ United), Michael Gogl (Alpecin-Premier Tech), Jasha Sütterlin (Jayco AlUla), Fabian Weiss (Tudor), Sinuhé Fernandez (Burgos Burpellet BH) and Ivan Cobo (Kern Pharma) have opened a gap at km 15.

headline: The gap increases
subtext: The six leaders are now riding 1'25'' ahead of the bunch.

headline: Dversnes in pursuit
subtext: Fredrik Dversnes (Uno-X Mobility) tries to make it a seven-man breakaway.

headline: The situation at km 20
subtext: Enzo Paleni (Groupama-FDJ United), Michael Gogl (Alpecin-Premier Tech), Jasha Sütterlin (Jayco AlUla), Fabian Weiss (Tudor), Sinuhé Fernandez (Burgos Burpellet BH) and Ivan Cobo (Kern Pharma) lead the way. +37'' Fredrik Dversnes (Uno-X Mobility) +1'38'' Peloton

headline: Dversnes joins the 6 leaders
subtext: After 22 km, Fredrik Dversnes (Uno-X Mobility) has bridged the gap to Enzo Paleni (Groupama-FDJ United), Michael Gogl (Alpecin-Premier Tech), Jasha Sütterlin (Jayco AlUla), Fabian Weiss (Tudor), Sinuhé Fernandez (Burgos Burpellet BH) and Ivan Cobo (Kern Pharma).

headline: Gap under control?
subtext: The peloton reach km 24 with a gap of 1'42''. The attackers' lead had previously gone up to 2 minutes.

headline: The gap increases again
subtext: At km 35, the peloton trail by 2'05''. Cofidis and Visma-Lease a Bike have been reported to be setting the pace.

headline: No GC threat in the breakaway
subtext: It's up to the sprinters' teams to control the day, as Enzo Paleni (Groupama-FDJ United) is the only rider within an hour of Enric Mas (Movistar) in GC: 50th, +58'21''.

headline: The first climb of the day
subtext: The leaders have pushed their advantage to 2'45'' ahead of the ascent up Puerto del Peralejo (5.2 km at 4.3%).

headline: 43.1 km in the first hour
subtext: The peloton are moving closer on the climb: 2'25'', compared to 2'55'' at the bottom.

headline: The attackers are done with the climb
subtext: The peloton trail by 2'20''.

headline: Results at Puerto del Peralejo (cat. 3, km 47.6)
subtext: 1. Paleni, 3 pts 2. Weiss, 2 pts 3. Fernandez, 1 pt

headline: Van Aert: “I always love to go in the breakaway but…”
subtext: Wout van Aert announced Visma-Lease a Bike's ambition to control the stage for a sprint: "I think that as a team we have the aim to control the stage, it's a hard one but the finish should suit us. It's always tricky if all the other teams have other ideas but our idea is to control the race. [For a bunch sprint?] Yes. I always love to go in the breakaway but you have to maximize your chances, and we think we have more chances by controlling the situation."

headline: Samitier: "A second chance with Bryan"
subtext: In line with Wou van Aert's quotes, Sergio Samitier also announced Cofidis were keenon a sprint for Bryan Coquard, the winner of stage 8: "Today we’ve got a second chance with Bryan, so let’s go for it. A win always takes the pressure off, but what’s done is done. There are still 12 stages to go and we can’t afford to relax – if more wins come our way, so much the better. It’s clear we’re not here just for a stroll; we’re going to contest every stage. I’m going to take it day by day, because I’ve seen what this second week has in store and it’s very tough. Day by day, today with Bryan, and then I’ll think about possible breakaways.” Samitier turned 31 yesterday.

headline: Ben Turner retires
subtext: The Brit is the second Netcompany Ineos to leave La Vuelta 26 after his compatriot Josh Tarling.

headline: Wout van Aert (Visma I Lease a Bike)
A stabilised situation
subtext: After 66 kilmetres, Enzo Paleni (Groupama-FDJ United), Michael Gogl (Alpecin-Premier Tech), Fredrik Dversnes (Uno-X Mobility), Jasha Sütterlin (Jayco AlUla), Fabian Weiss (Tudor), Sinuhé Fernandez (Burgos Burpellet BH) and Ivan Cobo (Kern Pharma) are riding 2'40'' ahead of the bunch.

headline: How to upset the field?
subtext: Earlier at La Vuelta 26, Fredrik Dversnes (Uno-X Mobility) gave some indisght based on his personal success in the Giro 2026. He's at the front to try and enforce them today: "It’s about having some bad days to lower other's expectations, then come in a breakaway with rather smaller guys that had much bigger engines than you think, and then you just hammer away and win."

headline: Onto the second climb
subtext: The peloton trail by 2'30'' at the bottom of the ascent up Puerto de Ayna (7.7 km at 4%).

headline: The breakaway holds a gap of just over 2 minute
The gap decreases again on the climb
subtext: The peloton move closer: 2'05''.

headline: 100 kilometres to go
subtext: The average speed after 2 hours: 42.1 km/h. The last gap: 1'48''. Sergio Samitier (Cofidis) is driving the bunch with Steven Kruijswijk (Visma-Lease a Bike) on his wheel.

headline: Visma | Lease a Bike and Cofidis leading the peloton
Samitier sets a very strong pace on the climb
subtext: The gap has decreased to 1'20'' as Cofidis try to hurt the legs of Bryan Coquard's rivals.

headline: Results at Puerto de Ayna (cat. 3, km 86.3)
subtext: 1. Weiss, 3 pts 2. Sütterlin, 2 pts 3. Fernandez, 1 pt

headline: September 1st is a landmark day for Slovenian cycling
subtext: Today marks: - the 20th anniversary of Slovenia’s first Grand Tour leader jersey, claimed by Janez Brajkovic in La Vuelta 2006 (stage 7, Puerto de El Morredero) - the 7th anniversary of Pogacar’s first Grand Tour stage win, in La Vuelta 19 (stage 9, Els Cortals d’Encamp) - the 6th anniversary of Primoz Roglic’s victory in Orcières-Merlette, in the Tour de France 2020 (stage 4) - the 5th anniversary of Primoz Roglic’s victory at Lagos de Covadonga, claiming the stage and La Roja four days before his third overall triumph in Santiago de Compostela.

headline: The gap increases again after the ascent
subtext: At km 102, the peloton trail by 1'40''.

headline: Back to (almost) 2 minutes
subtext: The seven leaders enter the final 75 kilomeres with a gap of 1'55''.

headline: Headed to Hellin
subtext: Hellin (km 125) has been a La Vuelta stage town on a handful of occasions, most recently in 2017. The race headed to Xorret de Cati, where Julian Alaphilippe took his first Grand Tour stage win.

headline: Birtdhay boy Svestad-Bardseng wants to "enjoy the day"
subtext: Embret Svestad-Bardseng (Netcompany Ineos) turns 24 today: “[I want to] enjoy the day. I just hope I don’t have a terrible day, basically; I hope the legs are good and I can enjoy the day. Maybe if a teammate wins, then we can enjoy the day. We’ve been focused [on Oscar Onley’s GC] the whole way. It’s the same focus now as it’s been the whole race. He’s looking better and better. He’s doing very well, so it just gives us confidence. We just have to keep going. We’ll have to support him and make him perform the best he can.”

headline: The peloton have accelerated again
subtext: The last gap: 1'35''. The attackers are one kilometre from the itnermediate sprint.

headline: Weiss is first at the intermediate sprint
subtext: The attackers just entered the final 60 kilometres with a lead of a minute and a half.

headline: Results at the intermediate sprint (Hellin, km 125)
subtext: 1. Weiss, 20 pts / 6’’ 2. Sütterlin, 17 pts / 4’’ 3. Gogl, 15 pts 4. Cobo, 13 pts 5. Paleni, 10 pts

headline: The average speed after 3 hours: 44.7 km/h
subtext: The pace seriously increased on more favourable terrain.

headline: Gogl suffers a mechanical
subtext: Austria's national champion rapidly returns to the breakaway group, 1'25'' ahead of the peloton.

headline: Into the final 40 kilometres
subtext: Magnus Cort (Uno-X Mobility) just returned to the bunch after a mechanical. The Danish all-rounder spoke at the start as he takespart in his last Grand Tour: "I feel ok, I have decent legs and the team is doing really well so I'm enjoying it a lot. We came here with the ambition to chase stages and we already won one, and there are opportunities left; we’re fighting and happy with what we got so far. I enjoyed many Vueltas and my first win on the Word Tour was also here ten years ago, I've always wanted to race it so I really wanted to come back."

headline: Heading for the final climb of the day
subtext: The seven leaders are five kilometres form the bottom of the ascent up Puerto de Socovos. The last gap: 1'22''.

headline: Down to 4 leaders
subtext: Enzo Paleni (Groupama-FDJ United), Michael Gogl (Pinarello Q36.5), Fredrik Dversnes (Uno-X Mobility) and Ivan Cobo (Kern Pharma) are about to begin the final ascent. Jasha Sütterlin (Jayco AlUla), Fabian Weiss (Tudor) and Sinuhé Fernandez (Burgos Burpellet BH) have been dropped on an uncategorised uphill section.

headline: Some moves in the bunch
subtext: Some attackers try to make the most of the rolling terrain ahead of the final climb. Matthew Brennan (Visma-Lease a Bike) reacts himself to cover their moves.

headline: Weiss returns to the front as the road rises
subtext: The attackers have just tackled the ascent of Puerto de Socovos (9.8km at 3.5%). The last gap to the bunch: 1'07''.

headline: Sivakov insists; Pedersen is distanced
subtext: Already named the most combative rider on Sunday, Pavel Sivakov (UAE Emirates XRG) is very active. Valentin Paret-Peintre (Soudal Quick-Step) also attacks. Cofidis try to control the situation. Mads Pedersen (Lidl-Trek) is among the riders off the back.

headline: A birthday boy on the move
subtext: On the ascent, Eddie Dunbar (Pinarello Q36.5) opens a small gap with Valentin Paret-Peintre (Soudal Quick-Step).

headline: Dunbar and Barta in pursuit
subtext: Eddie Dunbar (Pinarello Q36.5) has dropped Valentin Paret-Peintre (Soudal Quick-Step) and is about to be joined by Will Barta (Tudor). They are 45'' behind the five leaders, who face the final 5 kilometres of ascent. The reduced peloton trail by 1 minute.

headline: Gogl ups the ante into the final 25 kilometres
subtext: Weiss is dropped. Dunbar still trails by 40''. Barta is caught by the bunch (+55'').

headline: Vermaerke attacks; Mas reacts
subtext: As Richard Carapaz (EF Education-EasyPost) and Mattias Skjelmose (Lidl-Trek) followed a move initiated by Kevin Vermaerke (UAE Emirates XRG), Enric Mas (Movistar) moved to close the gap. There are around 20 riders in the bunch. They are half a minute behind the attackers with 23 km to go.

headline: Vermaerke goes again
subtext: This time, he's folloewed by Thibau Nys (Lidl-Trek). Matthew Brennann (Visma-Lease a Bike) bridges the gap with Tobias Johannessen (Uno-X Mobility). More chasers set off from the bunch.

headline: Dversnes leads the way to the final summit
subtext: Behind them, a new 4-man chase group has emerged: Vermaerke, Johannessen and Brennan are up there again, this time with Axel Laurance (Netcompany Ineos).

headline: Results at Puerto de Socovos (cat. 3, km 163.3)
subtext: 1. Dversnes, 3 pts 2. Gogl, 2 pts 3. Cobo, 1 pt

headline: The chasers are caught
subtext: The four leaders face the final 17 kilometres with a gap of 20 seconds.

headline: 2 leaders with 12 km to go
subtext: Gogl and Dversnes hold on to a 15'' gap.

headline: The final 10 kilometres
subtext: The last gap: 14 seconds.

headline: New moves on an uphill section with 7km to go
subtext: Gogl can't keep up with Dversnes at the front. The peloton still trail by 15 seconds. Counter-attackers try to make the jump.

headline: Elosegui has joined Dversnes at the front
subtext: Milan Vader (Pinarello Q36.5) tries to chase them. Sepp Kuss (Visma-Leasea Bike) is on his wheel.

headline: 4 leaders with 5 km to go
subtext: Kuss and Vader have bridged the gap. Vermaerke and Calzoni are just behind. Decathlon CMA CGM pull the bunch with minimal gaps.

headline: Calzoni goes solo into the final 4 km
subtext: The Italian puncheur has opened a gap. Visma-Lease a Bike try to react.

headline: Calzoni is caught with 2 km to go
subtext: Matthew Brennan sets the pace with Enric Mas on his wheel.

headline: Last kilometre
subtext: Jack Haig (Netcompany Ineos) drives the bunch.

headline: Bastien Tronchon wins stage 10 of La Vuelta 26!
subtext: What a finale! The Frenchman can't believe it!

headline: Top 5
subtext: 1. Bastien Tronchon (Groupama-FDJ United) 2. Magnus Cort (Uno-X Mobility) 3. Thibau Nys (Lidl-Trek) 4. Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) 5. Alessandro Romele (XDS Astana)
